extracted.intended_audience: employers, petitioners, dependents, designated school officials, Department of State and USCIS adjudicators, and nonimmigrant applicants (F, G, H classifications)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements for admitting, authorizing employment for, and adjudicating nonimmigrant classifications (F border commuters; G representatives/dependents; H temporary workers including H-1B/H-1C/H-2A/H-2B/H-3). Covers eligibility criteria, documentation, petitioning, portability, and limits on employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Border commuter student reduced course load authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated school official at the school may authorize an eligible border commuter student to enroll in a course load below that otherwise required for a full course of study provided that the reduced course load is consistent with the border commuter student's certified course of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to paragraph (f)(6) of this section; reduced course load must be consistent with the certified course of study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of admission for border commuter students
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1 nonimmigrant student admitted as a border commuter student will be admitted until a date certain; the DSO is required to specify a completion date on the Form I-20 that reflects the actual semester or term dates for the commuter student's current term of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new Form I-20 is required for each new semester or term. Provisions relating to duration of status and extension of stay (paragraphs (f)(5) and (f)(7)) are not applicable to border commuter students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Border commuter student employment restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A border commuter student may not be authorized to accept any employment in connection with his or her F-1 student status, except for curricular practical training as provided in paragraph (f)(10)(i) or post-completion optional practical training as provided in paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(A)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment is limited to specified CPT or post-completion OPT provisions only.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS fee remittance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien who applies for F-1 or F-3 nonimmigrant status to enroll in a program at an SEVP-certified institution is required to pay the SEVIS fee to DHS pursuant to 8 CFR 214.13, except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remittance of fee is a mandatory prerequisite tied to SEVP certification; see 8 CFR 214.13 for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of G classification (representatives to international organizations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination by a consular officer prior to admission and the recognition by the Secretary of State subsequent to admission is evidence of the proper classification of a nonimmigrant under section 101(a)(15)(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission and recognition serve as evidence of proper G classification; applicable to subsections (i)-(v) with differing admission periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of admission for G nonimmigrants
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien with nonimmigrant status under section 101(a)(15)(G)(i)-(iv) is to be admitted for the duration of recognition by the Secretary of State; an alien defined in 101(a)(15)(G)(v) is to be admitted for an initial period not more than three years and may be granted extensions not more than two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of temporary stay for G(v) must be accompanied by a statement signed by the employing official describing continued employment intent and type of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of dependent for G-1, G-3, G-4
rubrics_metrics.description: For employment purposes, 'dependent' of a G-1, G-3, or G-4 principal alien means immediate family habitually residing in the same household: (i) spouse; (ii) unmarried children under 21; (iii) unmarried sons/daughters under 23 in full-time post-secondary attendance; (iv) unmarried sons/daughters under 25 in full-time post-secondary attendance if pre-November 21, 1988 bilateral agreement applies and does not specify 23 as max age; (v) unmarried sons/daughters physically or mentally disabled who cannot care for themselves; (vi) immediate family members described in 22 CFR 41.21(a)(3)(i)-(iv) designated by DOS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of Protocol maintains listing of foreign states with applicable bilateral agreements; paragraph (g)(2) specifies documentation requirements for some categories (e.g., certification for disability, proof of full-time attendance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of formal bilateral agreement or de facto arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability of a formal bilateral agreement is based on the foreign state which employs the principal alien, not on nationality; applicability of an informal de facto arrangement is based on the foreign state which employs the principal alien but requires that the principal also be a national of that foreign state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of applicability affects whether dependents may be authorized to work under the bilateral/de facto provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax and jurisdiction responsibilities for employed G dependents
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependents granted employment authorization are responsible for payment of all federal, state and local income, employment and related taxes and Social Security contributions on any remuneration received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immunity from civil or administrative jurisdiction (e.g., Article 37 of the Vienna Convention) does not apply to these dependents with respect to matters arising out of their employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment authorization pursuant to formal bilateral agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependents of a G-1 or G-3 principal assigned to official duty may accept or continue unrestricted employment based on formal bilateral agreements if the agreement includes persons in G-1 or G-3 status, upon favorable recommendation by Department of State and issuance of employment authorization by the Service in accordance with 8 CFR part 274a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of Protocol maintains the listing of foreign states with formal bilateral employment agreements; application procedures are set in paragraph (g)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment authorization pursuant to informal de facto arrangements and G-4 dependents
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependents of a G-1 or G-3 principal may be authorized to accept or continue employment based on de facto arrangements, and dependents of a G-4 principal may be authorized upon favorable recommendation by Department of State and issuance of employment authorization in accordance with 8 CFR part 274a, provided conditions in paragraph (g)(5)(ii)(A)-(E) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include: (A) both principal and dependent maintain appropriate status; (B) principal assignment expected >6 months; (C) reciprocity (foreign government allows similar employment) not prohibited; (D) proposed employment not in DOL Schedule B or otherwise an oversupplied occupation (student part-time exception applies); (E) proposed employment not contrary to US interest (examples listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedures for G dependent employment (Form I-566 path)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dependent must submit a completed Form I-566 to Department of State through the office/mission/organization which employs the principal; required supporting documentation varies by dependent category (e.g., certified statement of full-time study, medical certification for disability, employer's statement with job description, salary, and verification of qualifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOS reviews and endorses Form I-566; if endorsement is favorable, dependent may apply to USCIS for employment authorization presenting the endorsed Form I-566 and any additional documentation required by the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of authorized employment for G dependents
rubrics_metrics.description: If approved, employment under this section shall be granted in increments of not more than three years each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization increment limits apply to subsequent extensions as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: No appeal from denial of G dependent employment permission
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be no appeal from a denial of permission to accept or continue employment under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denials are final under this provision; other administrative remedies are not provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: G-2 and G-5 dependents ineligible for employment under this section
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent or family member of a principal alien classified G-2 or G-5 may not be employed in the United States under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment authorization scheme applies only to G-1, G-3, and G-4 as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of unauthorized employment for G-classified aliens
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien classified under section 101(a)(15)(G) who is not a principal alien and who engages in employment outside the scope of, or in a manner contrary to this section, may be considered in violation of section 241(a)(1)(C)(i) of the Act; a principal alien who engages in employment outside the scope of his/her official position may also be considered in violation of that section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized employment can lead to statutory violations and immigration consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special provision limiting G-1 employment authorizations (historical)
rubrics_metrics.description: As of February 16, 1990 no new employment authorization will be granted and no pre-existing employment authorization will be extended for a G-1 dependent absent an appropriate bilateral agreement or de facto arrangement; a G-1 dependent with prior authorization may be allowed to continue until expiration, loss of dependent status, or March 19, 1990.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a historical cutoff provision with grandfathering conditions; consult current DOS listings for present applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer petition requirement for H classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 101(a)(15)(H) an alien may be authorized temporarily to perform services or receive training if petitioned for by the employer; the employer must file a petition with the Service for review of services/training and determination of the alien's eligibility before the alien may apply for a visa or seek admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This general rule applies to H-1C, H-1B, H-2A, H-2B, and H-3 classifications; paragraph sets forth standards and procedures applicable to these classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C classification definition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: H-1C applies to an alien coming temporarily to the U.S. to perform services as a registered nurse, meets section 212(m)(1) requirements, and will perform services at a facility for which DOL has certified an unexpired attestation under section 212(m)(2); classification expires 4 years from June 11, 2001.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facility and DOL attestation requirements are governed by 20 CFR part 655, subpart L and 20 CFR 655.1111.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B classification definition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: H-1B applies to an alien coming temporarily to perform services in a specialty occupation (per section 214(i)(1) and (i)(2)), or to perform services of exceptional nature for DOD cooperative projects, or to perform as a fashion model of distinguished merit and ability, and for whom the Secretary of Labor has determined and certified that the prospective employer filed a labor condition application under section 212(n)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H-1B classification requires compliance with labor condition application (LCA) certification and statutory specialty occupation definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A classification definition (agricultural temporary work)
rubrics_metrics.description: H-2A applies to an alien coming temporarily to the United States to perform agricultural work of a temporary or seasonal nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special agricultural provisions in paragraph (h)(5) apply; temporary labor certification required prior to petition filing per program rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2B classification definition (nonagricultural temporary work)
rubrics_metrics.description: H-2B applies to an alien coming temporarily to perform nonagricultural work of a temporary or seasonal nature if there are not sufficient U.S. workers able, willing, qualified, and available at time/place of application; requires a temporary labor certification issued by DOL or Governor of Guam prior to filing a petition with USCIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS may review the temporary or permanent nature of services described on the approved temporary labor certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-3 classification definition (trainee/special education exchange)
rubrics_metrics.description: H-3 applies to an alien coming temporarily as a trainee (other than graduate medical education/training or training provided primarily at or by an academic/vocational institution) or as a participant in a special education exchange program providing practical training and experience in educating children with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H-3 excludes certain educational training contexts (e.g., graduate medical education).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition filing requirements and form compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. employer seeking to classify an alien as H-1B, H-2A, H-2B, or H-3 must file a petition on the form prescribed by USCIS in accordance with the form instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must follow form instructions; some subparagraphs reserved; supporting documents (e.g., labor certification) required where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services or training for more than one employer
rubrics_metrics.description: If the beneficiary will perform nonagricultural services for, or receive training from, more than one employer, each employer must file a separate petition with USCIS as provided in the form instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple employers cannot be covered under a single petition; each must file and document terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of employers and authorization to begin employment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the alien is in the United States and seeks to change employers, the prospective new employer must file a petition requesting classification and an extension of stay; except as provided (paragraph (h)(2)(i)(I), 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(21), or section 214(n)), the alien is not authorized to begin employment with the new petitioner until the petition is approved. An H-1C nonimmigrant may not change employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portability exceptions and specific regulatory cross-references may allow work authorization upon filing in limited circumstances; H-1C change of employer is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended or new petition requirement for material changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must file an amended or new petition, with appropriate fee, to reflect any material changes in terms/conditions of employment or the beneficiary's eligibility as specified in the original approved petition; H-1B/H-2A/H-2B amended/new petition must be accompanied by a current or new DOL determination (including certified LCA for H-1B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended/new petition must be filed before material change occurs; beneficiary not authorized to work under materially changed terms until new/amended petition is approved unless eligible for portability.

rubrics_metrics.name: When amended/new petition is not required (H-1B exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner does not need to file an amended or new petition when: (i) moving beneficiary to a new job location within the same area of intended employment as listed on the certified LCA; (ii) placing beneficiary on short-term placements/assignments outside area of intended employment for total of 30 days or less in 1-year period (or 60 days under certain conditions); (iii) beneficiary going to a non-worksite location for employee development or peripatetic jobs where duties require frequent travel (peripatetic limits: not exceeding 5 consecutive workdays per visit, or 10 consecutive for workers who spend most time at one location).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes involving different geographical areas that require a corresponding LCA certification are considered material and require new/amended petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents as petitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. agent may file a petition for workers who are self-employed, use agents for short-term arrangements, or where a foreign employer authorizes the agent to act; an agent may be the actual employer, representative of both, or person/entity authorized by employer. The burden is on the agent to explain terms/conditions and provide required documentation; in questionable cases, a contract between employers and beneficiaries may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agent performing the function of an employer must guarantee wages and other terms/conditions by contractual agreement with the beneficiaries. Foreign employers using a U.S. agent remain responsible for complying with employer sanctions under section 274A and 8 CFR part 274a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple H-1B petitions restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer may not file more than one H-1B petition in the same fiscal year on behalf of the same alien if the alien is subject to numerical limits or exempt status; if an H-1B petition is denied (other than for fraud/misrepresentation), the employer may file a subsequent petition in same fiscal year provided numerical limit not reached or filing is exempt; otherwise multiple filings by same employer on same alien will result in denial or revocation of all such petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS may issue RFE/NOID/NOIR if related entities file multiple petitions and fail to demonstrate legitimate business need; related entities failing to demonstrate need may have all petitions denied/revoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B portability eligibility and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An eligible H-1B nonimmigrant is authorized to start concurrent or new employment under section 214(n) upon filing of a nonfrivolous H-1B petition on behalf of such alien (or as of requested start date), provided (1) the alien has been lawfully admitted in H-1B status; (2) a nonfrivolous H-1B petition for new employment has been filed before the alien's current authorized stay expires; (3) the alien has not been employed without authorization from last admission through filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment authorized under portability automatically ceases upon adjudication of the pending petition; successive portability petitions have special rules about adjudication, denials, and continuation of work under prior approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A and H-2B portability rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An eligible H-2A or H-2B nonimmigrant is authorized to start new employment upon proper filing of a nonfrivolous H-2A or H-2B petition requesting the same classification that the nonimmigrant currently holds, or as of the requested start date, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is defined similarly to H-1 portability: admission in classification, properly filed petition before current stay expires, and no unauthorized employment. Employment based on pending petition requires compliance with program requirements even if petition is later denied/withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of filing for H petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition filed under section 101(a)(15)(H) may not be filed earlier than 6 months before the date of actual need for the beneficiary's services or training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures petitions are filed in a timeframe reflecting actual need; exceptions not provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple beneficiaries rule (up to 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 25 named beneficiaries may be included in an H-1C, H-2A, H-2B, or H-3 petition if the beneficiaries will be performing the same service/receiving the same training for the same period and location; if more than 25 named beneficiaries, additional petition(s) required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If beneficiaries not fully identified at filing, unnamed beneficiaries may be shown by total number; USCIS may require naming H-2B beneficiaries to establish eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming beneficiaries requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: H-1B, H-1C, and H-3 petitions must include the name of each beneficiary. H-2A/H-2B petitions must include names of beneficiaries currently in the United States but need not name beneficiaries not currently in the U.S., except where USCIS requires names for eligibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple petitions for subsequent beneficiaries must include copy of the same temporary labor certification and reference previously filed petitions associated with that certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A petitions special agricultural criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Special criteria for admission, extension, and maintenance of status apply to H-2A petitions and are specified in paragraph (h)(5). Other provisions of §214.2(h) apply only to the extent they do not conflict with the special agricultural provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult paragraph (h)(5) for details on agricultural-specific requirements and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C 'registered nurse' definition and facility eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For H-1C classification, 'registered nurse' means person authorized by a State Board of Nursing to engage in RN practice in a state/territory and practicing at a facility which provides health care services. A facility (U.S. employer providing health care services) may file H-1C if it meets eligibility standards of 20 CFR 655.1111 and requirements of DOL regulations in 20 CFR part 655 subpart L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position must involve nursing practice and require licensure/authorization from State Board of Nursing in state of intended employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C beneficiary licensure and qualification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1C petition for a nurse shall be accompanied by evidence that the nurse: (A) has obtained a full and unrestricted license to practice nursing in the country where nursing education was obtained or has received nursing education in the U.S.; (B) has passed CGFNS exam or obtained a full and unrestricted permanent license to practice as an RN in the state of intended employment, or a permanent license in any U.S. state/territory plus temporary authorization in the state of intended employment; and (C) is fully qualified and eligible under laws governing the place of intended employment to practice as an RN immediately upon admission (temporary/interim licensing may be obtained after entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary or interim licensing may be obtained immediately after entry to meet state requirements for employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C petitioner documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioning facility shall submit with an H-1C petition: (A) a current copy of DOL's notice of acceptance of filing of its attestation on Form ETA 9081; (B) a statement describing any limitations which state/jurisdiction law place on the alien's services; (C) evidence that the named alien(s) meet the definition of registered nurse and satisfy requirements in section 212(m)(1) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must document DOL attestation acceptance, state licensing limitations, and beneficiary's qualifications per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C licensure conditions upon admission
rubrics_metrics.description: A nurse granted H-1C classification based on passage of the CGFNS exam must, upon admission to the U.S., be able to obtain temporary licensure or other temporary authorization to practice as an RN from the State Board of Nursing in the state of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An alien admitted on basis of temporary license/authorization must comply with state licensure requirements for RNs in the intended state of employment.
